setup: Stand tall with your feet between hip- and shoulder-width apart.
Place your hands on your hips or gently behind your head with your elbows flared wide.
Soften your knees slightly and engage your core to lock in a neutral spine.
steps: Initiate the movement by reaching your hips backward as if trying to touch a wall behind you.
Lower your torso forward while keeping your chest proud, spine straight, and knees softly bent at a fixed angle.
Continue hinging until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings or your torso approaches parallel to the floor.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to a fully upright standing position.
instructions.breathing: Inhale deeply and brace your core as you hinge forward; exhale as you drive your hips forward to stand.
cues: Keep your back flat and chest proud
Hinge at the hips, do not squat

common_faults.fault: Rounding the lower back during the descent.
common_faults.correction: Brace the abdominals and limit your depth to only as far as you can maintain a flat, neutral spine.

common_faults.fault: Bending the knees excessively into a squat.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a soft, static knee bend and focus entirely on horizontal hip displacement backward.

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending the lumbar spine at the top of the movement.
common_faults.correction: Finish the rep by squeezing your glutes to stand tall without arching your lower back backward.

precautions: Stop the descent if your hamstrings feel excessively tight or if your lower back begins to round.

name: Bodyweight Good Morning
summary: A standing bodyweight hip-hinge exercise that reinforces posterior chain mechanics while strengthening the glutes, hamstrings, and spinal erectors.
